membership_order: state.findByType holds the declared aliases (or name:<name>) of FindObjectsByType<CreationOwnershipTracker>(FindObjectsInactive.Include, FindObjectsSortMode.None), sorted ordinally by alias; the returned order is in raw_output under the same seq. Scene roots keep GetRootGameObjects order. Nothing else is sorted, renamed or renumbered.
points_doc: tN.a.start: the first sceneUnloaded of transition N; t1.a.i..iii: after each creation in that handler; t1.a.iv: after the creation in the destroyer's OnDestroy; t2.a.made: after CreateScene("Made") + SetActiveScene in t2's handler; tN.b: the first sceneLoaded of tN; tN.c: the first controller LateUpdate after it. t1 = LoadScene(Extra, Single), t2 = LoadScene(Main, Single), t3 = LoadScene(Extra, Single).

contract.rule: Two repeats publish only if each satisfies every predicate below against its own trace and their canonical forms (contract.py) are byte-identical. The canonical form is the main output with exactly the three families below rewritten; every other row and leaf is copied unchanged and compared strictly. Raw outputs (main, raw_output, teardown_output) are kept as captured; nothing is widened after a capture.

outgoing-roots-destruction-prefix.where: the snapshot at point t1.a.iv (inside the destroyer's OnDestroy): state.scenes[ref = the scene t1.a.start reports unloaded].roots and .rootCount
predicates: teardown_output holds one 'attached' row per teardown-witnessed root, all at stage setup, and their 'name:<name>' refs are exactly the roots of that scene at point setup that carry no declared alias
every attached root has exactly one 'OnDestroy' row, at stage t1, in that scene, with mainSeq <= the seq of the t1.a.start snapshot (destroyed before the scene's sceneUnloaded)

the observed roots equal the setup roots in setup order minus exactly the witnessed roots whose OnDestroy mainSeq <= the seq of the t1.a.iv snapshot (the set destroyed so far in this repeat's own trace), and rootCount equals their number
outgoing-roots-destruction-prefix.canonical: roots -> {"contract": "destruction-prefix", "unwitnessed": the observed roots that carry no teardown witness, in observed order (strict)}; rootCount -> "contract:destruction-prefix"; a contract row after the source row lists the destroyed witnessed roots as a sorted set

not-cleaned-up-error-names.where: log rows with at Error whose message starts with the header
not-cleaned-up-error-names.header:
Some objects were not cleaned up when closing the scene. (Did you spawn new GameObjects from OnDestroy?)
The following scene GameObjects were found:
predicates: message == header + each name + "\n", at least one name, no name repeated
not-cleaned-up-error-names.canonical: message -> {"header": header, "names": the names sorted ordinally (an unordered set)}

inter-object-cleanup-order.where: stage t2: the lifecycle rows OnDisable/OnDestroy of the made aliases before the t2.a.start snapshot
predicates: they form one contiguous block of seqs with no other row inside it
every made alias has exactly one OnDisable and one OnDestroy there, OnDisable first (strict per object)
none of them has an OnDisable/OnDestroy row in stage t2 after the t2.a.start snapshot (destruction before the owning scene's sceneUnloaded)
inter-object-cleanup-order.canonical: the block's rows sorted by (alias in declared order, OnDisable before OnDestroy), renumbered with the block's own seqs; every other field of each row is unchanged; the contract row records whether each OnDisable was immediately followed by the same object's OnDestroy (strict)

contract.strict: Ownership, existence, scene membership, parent/root, Find/FindObjectsByType membership (sorted), light probes, per-object message order and every row outside the three families stay strict. The raw FindObjectsByType order (raw_output) and the teardown_output order are recorded, not compared.
